Report_ID: Incidence of Grade II, III diarrhea (NCI CTC v2.0)
Title: Randomized controlled trial of live lactobacillus acidophilus plus bifidobacterium bifidum in prophylaxis of diarrhea during radiotherapy in cervical cancer patients
Author: Chitapanarux et al.
Comment: The paper reports the p-value but not the chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom, relative effect estimate, or confidence interval; these fields were left null. Percentages are reported rounded, while event counts are explicit in Table 2.
domain: Oncology supportive care; radiation-induced diarrhea prophylaxis
Study Environment: Pelvic radiotherapy with concurrent weekly cisplatin
Participant type: Patients with FIGO stage IIB–IIIB squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix receiving concurrent chemoradiotherapy
Outcome measurement: NCI CTC version 2.0, assessed weekly; grade 2 was an increase of 4–6 stools/day or nocturnal stools, and grade 3 was an increase of at least 7 stools/day, incontinence, or need for parenteral support for dehydration
Outcome variable: Incidence of Grade II, III diarrhea (NCI CTC v2.0)
outcome_family: incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea

Report_ID: Incidence of diarrhea grades 2 and 3 during treatment
Title: Effects of Probiotics with or without Honey on Radiation-induced Diarrhea
Author: Mansouri-Tehrani, Rabbani Khorasgani, and Roayaei
Comment: The paper reports cumulative grade 2-3 event counts but no direct relative effect estimate, confidence interval, or p-value for this cumulative probiotic-versus-placebo incidence comparison. The placebo arm is shared with the probiotic-plus-honey comparison and must not be double-counted in synthesis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Probiotic') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: Radiation Oncology Clinic at Sayyed-Al-Shohada Hospital
Participant type: Adult patients with pelvic cancers receiving radiotherapy
Recruitment source: Radiation Oncology Clinic at Sayyed-Al-Shohada Hospital, Isfahan, Iran
Outcome measurement: Common Toxicity Criteria of the National Cancer Institute; grade 2 = increase of 4-6 stools per day or nocturnal stools; grade 3 = increase of 7-9 stools per day or incontinence
Outcome variable: Incidence of diarrhea grades 2 and 3 during treatment
outcome_family: incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea

Report_ID: Freedom from moderate-to-severe radiation-induced diarrhoea (WHO grades 2–4) at 60 days
Title: A randomized double-blind controlled trial: Impact of probiotics on diarrhea in patients treated with pelvic radiation
Author: Demers, Dagnault, and Desjardins
Comment: The 17% and 35% values are Kaplan–Meier proportions remaining free of grade 2–4 diarrhoea at 60 days, not raw incidence proportions or event counts. Raw grade 2–4 event counts for the full cohort and an HR confidence interval were not reported. The high-dose arm was excluded from this pairwise row and is listed in additional_group_ns; the overall three-group curve comparison was p=0.13.
domain: Oncology supportive care; radiation-induced diarrhoea prevention
Study Environment: Single-center University Health Center, Hôtel-Dieu de Québec
Medium: Oral probiotic capsules administered during radiotherapy
Participant type: Adults with pelvic cancer receiving radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy
Recruitment source: University Health Center, Hôtel-Dieu de Québec
Outcome measurement: Daily digestive symptom log translated by a registered dietician into WHO diarrhoea grades; Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression analysis of time to first grade 2–4 diarrhoea
Outcome variable: Freedom from moderate-to-severe radiation-induced diarrhoea (WHO grades 2–4) at 60 days
additional_group_ns: High-dose Bifilact probiotics (10 billion CFU three times daily): n=59
outcome_family: incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea

Report_ID: Primary efficacy criterion: nonresponse due to Grade 2 or greater diarrhea, need for rescue with loperamide, or withdrawal because of lack of efficacy
Title: Effects of Probiotic Lactobacillus casei DN-114 001 in Prevention of Radiation-Induced Diarrhea: Results From Multicenter, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Nutritional Trial
Author: Giralt et al.
Comment: The extracted counts are for the paper's prespecified composite nonresponse endpoint, not Grade 2-or-higher diarrhea alone: an event could also be triggered by loperamide rescue or withdrawal for lack of efficacy. The paper does not report a separate pure Grade 2-or-higher diarrhea incidence count. The p = 0.568 is explicitly attached to this composite endpoint in the abstract/Figure 1; no chi-square statistic or relative effect estimate is reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Active probiotic drink containing Lactobacillus casei DN-114 001') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Design Type: Multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled two-arm parallel clinical trial
domain: Oncology supportive care; prevention of pelvic radiotherapy-induced diarrhea
Participant type: Women with gynecologic cancer receiving pelvic radiotherapy, with weekly cisplatin for cervical cancer
Recruitment source: Radiation oncology departments at participating hospitals in Spain
Outcome measurement: National Cancer Institute Common Toxicity Criteria, version 2.0, plus recorded loperamide rescue use and withdrawal for lack of efficacy
Outcome variable: Primary efficacy criterion: nonresponse due to Grade 2 or greater diarrhea, need for rescue with loperamide, or withdrawal because of lack of efficacy
